questions.prompt: Bonevac’s rhetorical aim in the skepticism lecture is to argue you:
choices: A Know everything with certainty.
B Know nothing—and that it may not even be reasonable to hold beliefs.
C Should only trust astrology.
D Must accept Plato’s Forms without argument.

questions.prompt: Why did Plato’s Academy students turn skeptical?
choices: A They preferred Aristotle’s ethics exclusively.
B They saw no way to explain knowledge of the Forms.
C The library burned and they quit philosophy.
D Skepticism was banned in Athens.

questions.prompt: Cicero’s “inapprehensibility” point is that perception itself lacks:
choices: A Any sensory content.
B An internal mark proving it is veridical.
C Relation to language.
D Connection to memory.

questions.prompt: The criterion problem he stresses is that there is:
choices: A Always a perfect neutral arbiter available.
B No neutral arbiter—hence pressure for a criterion that itself needs justification.
C Only mathematical criteria for ethics.
D No disagreement among observers ever.

questions.prompt: For Sextus Empiricus, suspension of judgment leads to:
choices: A Greater anxiety.
B Peace of mind.
C Mandatory political activism.
D Instant scientific discovery.
